curated.model: omr/8074-1 Universal Set with Flex System.mpd
curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8074-1/ (scans; the model file builds the tower crane, pages 12-24: the tower in steps 1-7 on pages 12-15, the cab and counter-jib in steps 1-9 on pages 16-18, then steps 8-13 on pages 19-24; the other pages are the front loader, the excavator and the forklift)

functions.does: The handwheel with the half-pin handle, low on the tower's side, winds the winch: its 12-long axle across the bottom of the tower is the drum, and the string runs up through the tower and the turntable, along the jib and down the arm at the jib's tip to the hook's pulley, raising or lowering the hook.
functions.source: book: tower steps 4 (12-long drum axle and string), 6-7 (handwheel and handle), step 13 (the string round the hook's pulley, inset); the cover draws an up-and-down arrow by the hook

functions.does: A pawl on the tower, a 4-long axle hanging from a pin, rests on the 16-tooth gear on the winch's axle so the hook can't run down by itself; lifting it lets the winch unwind.
functions.source: book: tower step 7 (the pawl, inset) and step 6; inferred: that it's a ratchet, from how it's built
functions.skip: a ratchet only matters under gravity

functions.does: The round yellow knob high on the tower's side slews the crane: its 6-long axle turns a 14-tooth bevel gear, which turns a vertical 4-long axle whose 8-tooth gear runs round the turntable's teeth, so the whole cab, counter-jib and jib turn on top of the tower.
functions.source: book: tower step 5 (sub-steps 3-5: the bevel gear, and the 4-long axle with its 8-tooth gear beside the turntable), step 7 (the knob, inset)

functions.does: One handwheel at the back of the counter-jib luffs the jib: its 10-long axle's worm turns a 24-tooth gear on a 12-long axle, whose two levers push two Flex System cables forward to a rocker of liftarms on the jib's pivot, and two short links from the rocker raise or lower the jib.
functions.source: book: cab steps 3 (the two worms on 10-long axles), 5 (handwheels), 6 (24-tooth gears and levers), steps 9-11 (the rocker, the two 5.6 cm cables and the jib); inferred: that this cable train luffs the jib rather than the arm, from how the parts are joined; the cover shows the jib raised

functions.does: The other handwheel at the back of the counter-jib swings the arm that hangs from the jib's tip: its worm turns a 24-tooth gear on an 8-long axle, whose two levers push a Flex System cable to a crank on the jib's pivot, and from there a long cable along the jib pushes the lever at the top of the arm, swinging the arm (and the hook hanging from it) in and out.
functions.source: book: cab steps 3, 5-6 and 8 (the 4 cm and 7.2 cm cables), steps 12 (the arm on its 8-long axle at the jib's tip, and the 10.4 cm cable along the jib) and 13; the cover shows the arm swung up
functions.note: worms hold both cable trains still when the handwheels aren't turned

questions.question: Does one cable train luff the jib and the other swing the tip arm?
